summary: S. 4949, the Water Resources Development Act of 2026, authorizes and modifies water resources development projects administered by the Army Corps of Engineers and programs administered by the Environmental Protection Agency. The bill provides authorizations for feasibility studies, ecosystem restoration, flood risk management, navigation, and environmental infrastructure projects across the United States. It also establishes new grant programs, reauthorizes funding for drinking water and wastewater infrastructure programs, requires various reports and briefings for Congress, and sets rules regarding Corps of Engineers project reviews, non-Federal contributions, and deauthorizations.

affected_groups.effect: Receive authority to request feasibility studies, contribute funds for projects, carry out certain operation and maintenance activities with credit or reimbursement, and enter into partnerships for flood and coastal storm risk management.
affected_groups.group: State and local governments and non-Federal project sponsors

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for reduced non-Federal cost shares (frequently set at 10 percent) for specific environmental infrastructure, western rural water, and flood risk management projects.

Eligible for federal grants, technical assistance, and loan fund allocations for drinking water safety, lead service line replacement, emerging contaminant treatment, cybersecurity, and digital infrastructure.
affected_groups.group: Public water systems and treatment works

affected_groups.effect: Impacted by authorizations, maintenance provisions, and deauthorizations concerning federal navigation channels, locks, dams, harbors, and inland waterways.

key_provisions: Authorizes numerous new feasibility studies and modifications for water resources development projects across multiple states, including navigation, flood risk management, and ecosystem restoration.

Authorizes specific construction and implementation projects for navigation, flood risk management, ecosystem restoration, and hurricane and storm damage risk reduction, along with associated cost estimates.
Reauthorizes and adjusts funding levels for environmental infrastructure programs, establishing new project authorities and modifying existing cost-shares for economically disadvantaged communities.
Modifies drinking water and clean water state revolving loan funds, authorizing appropriations for fiscal years 2027 through 2030 and expanding fund uses to address emerging contaminants like PFAS.
Establishes a digital infrastructure technology grant program and a point-of-use filtration system distribution pilot program administered by the Environmental Protection Agency.

Amends regulations and procedures governing Corps of Engineers project reviews, continuing authority programs, non-Federal contributions, and deauthorizations of designated navigation channels and flood control structures.
Requires the Secretary of the Army and the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to submit various reports, briefings, and implementation plans to designated congressional committees.
